key_insight: Tree-based machine learning can accurately predict band gaps across diverse halide perovskites and reveals that B-site and X-site chemistry dominate the trend.
engineering_relevance: These models can accelerate lead-free perovskite screening by linking composition and structure to target band gaps before costly experiments.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based regressors: Random Forest, GBRT, and XGB.
Used atomic and structural descriptors spanning A, B, and X site properties.
Ranked feature importance to identify the most influential band-gap drivers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy across multiple perovskite families, supported by model evaluation and feature-importance analysis.
watch_item: Predictive performance may depend on the available composition space and descriptor quality, so extrapolation to unseen chemistries should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
